songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Oct‑10 show erupts with blazing Crazy Fingers → Lost Sailor → Saint sequence
ai_show_review.blurb: The Frost Amphitheatre concert is a high‑energy romp highlighted by a scorching Crazy Fingers > Lost Sailor > Saint of Circumstance run and a crisp, soaring Take on Looks Like Rain. Jerry’s tone is razor‑sharp, Brent’s organ drives the jams, and Phil’s bass anchors every transition. Multiple soundboard and audience sources capture the set in excellent condition, making it a must‑listen for any Deadhead.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds on October 10, 1982 at Frost is pure Brent‑era fire. The first set builds with a tight New Minglewood Blues into Sugaree and a punchy Little Red Rooster before rolling into a bright Tennessee Jed and Cassidy that set the stage for an inspired Loser and a beautifully melodic Far From Me > Looks Like Rain transition. The second set ignites when Playing In The Band launches straight into Crazy Fingers, which morphs seamlessly into Lost Sailor > Saint of Circumstance – a sequence that many reviewers flag as the night’s centerpiece, with Jerry shredding in machine‑gun fashion and Brent laying down a soaring B‑3 solo. From there the band rides a rolling wave through Touch of Grey, a tight Drums/Space pair, The Wheel, Throwing Stones, and a rousing Black Peter > Sugar Magnolia finale that spills into an encore of (I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction and It’s All Over Now Baby Blue. Across the dozen recordings, the soundboard tapes from Miller’s 24‑bit fixed master stand out for their crystalline clarity and balanced mix, while several audience captures (especially the Sony ECM‑220T mics) rival them in warmth and presence. Together they paint a picture of a band locked in, with every member contributing to an electric, cohesive whole.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear 24‑bit soundboard with superb instrument separation and minimal hiss, delivering the most faithful representation of the band’s high‑energy performance.

key_highlights: Blazing Crazy Fingers > Lost Sailor > Saint of Circumstance sequence
Crisp, soaring Take on Looks Like Rain
Brent’s organ solo on New Minglewood Blues and tight jams on Far From Me
Exciting double encore that closes with Satisfaction and Baby Blue
song_highlights: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia is on fire throughout – razor‑sharp leads, machine‑gun solos on Loser and Sugar Magnolia, and a generally great tone; a few audience tapes note a slightly weak vocal on Baby Blue.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh delivers booming, low‑freq pulse that drives the jams, especially evident on Minglewood and during the Drums/Space segment; many recordings praise his ‘bomb‑dropping’ presence.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocals are emotive and energetic, highlighted by a Mick Jagger‑style swagger on Satisfaction and strong crowd‑lead sing‑alongs on Baby Blue and Morning Dew.
band_performance.Brent: Mydland’s B‑3 organ shines with fiery solos (notably the Minglewood jam) and textured fills that lift every transition; his keyboard work is consistently praised across all sources.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart locks in tight, driving beats that keep the band blazing, especially during the double encore and high‑intensity second‑set peaks.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann provides a steady, propulsive foundation, complementing Mickey’s rhythms and reinforcing Phil’s bass groove throughout.
